keys.description: The numeric counterpart of overlapDays: the value subtracted from a NON-DATE watermark's aggregate before it bounds the source read, so the target probe emits 'MAX([col]) - <lookback>' instead of a bare 'MAX([col])' (ProbeMaxAsync, IncrementalWindowResolver.cs:334-342) and, when fetchMinValuesFromSource widens the window, 'MIN(col) - <lookback>' on the source in the source dialect's quoting as well (ProbeMinAsync, IncrementalWindowResolver.cs:385-393), so both sides shift by the same amount and the comparison stays symmetric. Like the DATEADD it mirrors, the shift is applied to the aggregate inside the probe rather than to the predicate afterwards, so the watermark value a run reports is the value the read was actually bounded by. Applies ONLY to marks stamped IsDate false (the incremental.columns entries); the dateColumn mark keeps its overlapDays DATEADD and ignores this key entirely, and a flow that declares both gets each shift on its own mark. Why a numeric watermark needs a rewind at all: a monotonic key is monotonic in the order ids are ALLOCATED, not the order rows become VISIBLE, so a source that hands out an identity/auto-increment value at INSERT but publishes the row at COMMIT lets a reader see id N+k while N is still in flight; a bare MAX advances past N and the next run's strict '>' can never reach back down to it, so the row is skipped permanently and silently (in the estate the loss shows up as contiguous blocks of missing ids, each starting at exactly the previous run's watermark plus one). Size it in KEY UNITS, not days: comfortably above the number of ids that can be in flight at once. The re-read window it opens is reconciled by the keyed upsert, so a keyed flow re-reads rows it already holds and inserts nothing new; a KEYLESS flow (no load.keyColumns) appends the re-read rows again, which is the one configuration where a lookback duplicates data. The shift is silently SKIPPED, with no warning and no error, for a watermark column arithmetic does not apply to: only tinyint, smallint, int, bigint, decimal, numeric, money and smallmoney receive it, so a string, binary, rowversion or approximate (float/real) high-water column keeps its bare MAX rather than being fed a subtraction the source would reject (NumericLookback, IncrementalWindowResolver.cs:519-536). A value of 0 or less is inert and reproduces the bare MAX.

keys.validation: Unparseable value: FlowValidationException "<source>: 'initLoad.toDate' must be a date like 2024-01-31, got '<value>'." (YamlDocumentParts.ParseDate, invoked as ParseDate(y.ToDate, "initLoad.toDate", source) at src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:405).

keys.default: { keyColumns: [], skipUpdateExisting: false, skipInsertNew: false, matchKeysInSourceAndTarget: false, batchUpsert: false, batchUpsertRowCount: 2000, dataSetColumn: null, reloadColumn: null, streamData: true, threads: null, keepStagingTable: false, truncateStagingOnCompletion: false }
keys.description: Optional block controlling the ingestion load stage: the business key for the keyed upsert, skip flags, the delete-detection toggle, batching/dataset-loop knobs, and staging-table lifecycle. Binds to IngestionLoadYaml and is mapped by YamlIngestionFlowLoader.MapLoad to SqlFlow.Core.Ingestion.IngestionLoadPolicy (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:263-286); when the whole block is absent, MapLoad still runs and returns IngestionLoadPolicy's defaults verbatim, so 'load:' present-but-empty and 'load' entirely absent are identical. An empty keyColumns list (the default) routes the whole flow through the keyless append-only insert-all path instead of the keyed upsert (IngestionFlowRunner.BuildLoadStatements, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:853-857).

keys.appliesWhen: a keyed flow; no effect on a keyless flow
keys.description: Applies the keyed upsert through key-windowed batches (the legacy #UpdateKeys/#InsertKeys pattern) instead of one set-based statement per branch, so each DML stays under the lock-escalation threshold, with each window committing and releasing its locks on its own. Consumed as UpsertOptions.BatchToAvoidLockEscalation (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:915), which selects UpsertGenerator's BatchedUpdateScript/BatchedInsertScript, or the dataset-partitioned loop's batched inner loop, instead of the plain UPDATE/INSERT text (UpsertGenerator.cs:201-215,238-252,428-505). It also changes the load's transaction shape at the runner level: IngestionFlowRunner.ApplyLoadAsync is called with 'useTransaction: !flow.Load.BatchUpsertToAvoidLockEscalation' (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:427), so turning this on removes the single enclosing transaction around the whole apply, trading all-or-nothing atomicity for lock friendliness on large deltas. Has no effect on a keyless flow: the insert-all statement is always a single unbatched INSERT regardless of this setting.

keys.appliesWhen: load.batchUpsert is true
keys.description: Rows per key-window batch when load.batchUpsert is on. Consumed as UpsertOptions.BatchRowCount (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:916), sizing the '@Start'/'@End' window stride in UpsertGenerator's BatchedUpdateScript and BatchedInsertScript (UpsertGenerator.cs:600-611,634-645) and the '@Batch' stride in the dataset-partitioned loop's batched inner loop (UpsertGenerator.cs:507-510). Ignored when load.batchUpsert is false, and ignored on a keyless flow.
keys.validation: "BatchRowCount must be at least 1, got {value}." (UpsertGenerator.cs:149), enforced only when load.batchUpsert is true. Since the YAML mapper only null-coalesces ('y.BatchUpsertRowCount ?? 2000', YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:277), an explicit 0 or negative value survives loading and fails only when the upsert is generated at run time with batching on.

keys.default: null (no dataset-partitioned loop; the plain set-based upsert runs)
keys.appliesWhen: a keyed flow (load.keyColumns or matchKeys.keyColumns non-empty)
keys.description: When set, the keyed upsert is applied one dataset at a time, partitioned by this column's distinct values in ascending order: staging is first deduplicated to one row per (dataset, key), then each dataset's UPDATE-then-INSERT runs against the target as the prior datasets left it, so a business key recurring across datasets ends at the value from the last dataset carrying it. Generated by UpsertGenerator.GenerateDataSetLoopStatement as one combined script (UpsertGenerator.cs:184-186,368-554) instead of separate UPDATE/INSERT statements, reporting its Inserts/Updates totals as one result-set row. Consumed as UpsertOptions.DataSetColumn, set from 'MapNameOrNull(nameMap, flow.Load.DataSetColumn) ?? flow.Load.DataSetColumn' (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:923-925), i.e. mapped to the cleaned target column name when column-name cleanup renamed it. Distinct from the similarly named source.dataSetColumn (IngestionEndpointYaml.DataSetColumn), which instead feeds the canonical dataset index on a newly-created target (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:365) and is unrelated to this upsert-loop behavior. Honors load.batchUpsert/load.batchUpsertRowCount within each dataset iteration. Has no effect on a keyless flow. The YAML value is trimmed and blank-normalized to null at load time ('string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(y.DataSetColumn) ? null : y.DataSetColumn.Trim()', YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:278), unlike most other optional strings in this document (confirmed via YamlDocumentParts.NullIfBlank, which blank-checks but does not trim).
keys.validation: "A dataset-column load (DataSetColumn) cannot be combined with SCD2 versioning." (UpsertGenerator.cs:156, when versioning.scd2.enabled is also true) and "DataSetColumn '<value>' is not among the data columns." (UpsertGenerator.cs:161, when the possibly name-mapped value does not case-insensitively match a bulk-copied target column name). Both are run-time checks raised when the upsert is generated, not at YAML load time.

keys.description: Keeps the flow's canonical staging table after a SUCCESSFUL run instead of dropping it (a FAILED run always keeps its staging table for debugging, regardless of this flag; the next run's rebuild resets a kept table either way). Consumed directly in IngestionFlowRunner ('if (!flow.Load.KeepStagingTable)'): when false (the default), both the staging table and, if the key-match pass ran, its canonical mkey_ key table are dropped with 'DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ...' after a successful run; when true, the staging table is left in place (optionally truncated, see load.truncateStagingOnCompletion) and the match-key table is also left undropped.

Business key column names (as they appear among the bulk-copied SOURCE columns) that identify a row for the update/insert match. Consumed as IngestionLoadPolicy.KeyColumns (IngestionPolicies.cs:12). Whenever this list is non-empty (and not overridden, see matchKeys.keyColumns), it becomes the 'effective key' (IngestionFlowRunner.EffectiveKeyColumns, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:817-820) used everywhere a business key is needed: the schema-evolution critical-mismatch gate, where a key, hash-key, identity, or primary-key column with an incompatible type change is flagged CRITICAL rather than silently widened (passed as 'KeySet(EffectiveKeyColumns(flow))' at IngestionFlowRunner.cs:340 into SchemaEvolutionPlanner.IsCritical, SchemaEvolutionPlanner.cs:112-115, independently confirmed: IsCritical returns true for a HashKey/Identity-role column, a primary-key column, or any column named in the key set); the two-step upsert's key-equality join and its per-row change-detection scope (UpsertGenerator.GenerateStatements, passed verbatim as UpsertOptions.KeyColumns, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:906); and, name-mapped to target column names via the bulk-copy column map, the canonical key index built on a newly-created target and, when versioning.scd2 is enabled, its filtered-unique SCD2 key-index variant (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:359-369,378-393). An empty list routes the flow through the keyless insert-all path instead (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:853-857), which ignores skipUpdateExisting/skipInsertNew/batchUpsert*/dataSetColumn entirely and always appends every staged row.
keys.validation: Load time: "'<source>': 'versioning.scd2' requires 'load.keyColumns' (the business key the dimension versions by)." (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:123-131, when versioning.scd2.enabled is true and this list is empty). Run time: "MatchKeysInSourceAndTarget is on, but the flow has no key columns (set load.keyColumns or matchKeys.keyColumns)." (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:669-671, when load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true and the effective key list is empty). Also run time, at upsert generation: "An upsert requires at least one key column." (UpsertGenerator.cs:135, unreachable via YAML because the keyless path is taken first when this list is empty) and "Key column '<key>' is not among the data columns." (UpsertGenerator.cs:143, when an entry does not case-insensitively match a bulk-copied target column name; this list is passed to the upsert as-is, never name-mapped, so it can diverge from cleaned target names).

keys.description: Turns on the post-load key-match (deleted-row detection) pass: after the upsert, the full distinct SOURCE key set is landed in the flow's canonical mkey_ work table (in the raw schema, rebuilt per run) and anti-joined against the target, so a target row whose key no longer exists in the source is tagged or deleted per matchKeys.action (IngestionFlowRunner.RunMatchKeysAsync, invoked at IngestionFlowRunner.cs:463 only when this flag is true). It also selects which key columns are 'effective' everywhere a business key is used: when true and matchKeys.keyColumns is non-empty, matchKeys.keyColumns overrides load.keyColumns for the upsert, the schema-evolution key set, and the canonical/SCD2 index planning (EffectiveKeyColumns, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:817-820); otherwise load.keyColumns is used regardless of this flag. At YAML load time, when this is true and matchKeys.action resolves to Tag (its default), the loader force-enables systemColumns.deletedDate to true even if the YAML explicitly set it to false (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:173-176; pinned by test YamlIngestionMatchKeysTests.TagMode_AutoEnableOverridesExplicitFalseOnDeletedDate, confirmed to exist in tests/SqlFlow.Core.Tests/YamlIngestionMatchKeysTests.cs), because Tag mode's soft delete stamps DeletedDate_DW.
keys.validation: This flag itself has no load-time validation; it gates the run-time checks described under load.keyColumns and systemColumns.deletedDate ("MatchKeysInSourceAndTarget is on, but the flow has no key columns ..." and "MatchKeys Tag mode soft-deletes by stamping DeletedDate_DW; enable the DeletedDate_DW system column.", both in IngestionFlowRunner.RunMatchKeysAsync, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:669-677).

keys.default: null (no per-file replace; the normal keyed upsert or keyless insert-all runs)
keys.description: Per-file (per-dataset) full replace: the column identifying a source file/dataset, typically FileName_DW (set the pre flow's showPathWithFileName so it carries the full path, the collision-free identity, and the provenance columns ride through the [pre].[v<Table>] view onto this ods target). When set, the load becomes a purge-then-insert scoped to the incoming batch instead of a keyed upsert: before inserting, the engine deletes every target row whose reloadColumn value is present in the staged batch (a set-based 'DELETE trg ... WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM <staging> src WHERE src.[col] = trg.[col])', NULL-safe so rows with no file identity are never touched), then inserts the staged rows. A resent file therefore fully replaces its prior version, including records the new version dropped (which a keyed upsert would leave orphaned), while files absent from this run's batch stay untouched; combined with incremental (on FileDate_DW), only the resent file is read into staging, so only that file is purged and reloaded. Consumed at IngestionFlowRunner.BuildLoadStatements before the keyless check (works with or without load.keyColumns), name-mapped to the cleaned target column like dataSetColumn, and generated by UpsertGenerator as a Purge statement plus an insert (deduped to one row per key when load.keyColumns are declared, so a key recurring across the batch's files cannot violate the target's unique key; insert-all otherwise). The purge and insert always run in one transaction (the runner forces it, even under load.batchUpsert), so a resend is atomic. Purged rows are reported as RowsDeleted. On the run that creates the target, an NCI_ReloadColumn nonclustered index is added so the purge seeks (skipped when the column is already the leading column of the key/date/dataset index).
keys.appliesWhen: any flow (keyed or keyless); it supersedes the keyed upsert
keys.validation: Load time (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs): rejected when combined with load.dataSetColumn ("'load.reloadColumn' (per-file replace) cannot be combined with 'load.dataSetColumn' ..."), versioning.scd2.enabled ("... cannot be combined with 'versioning.scd2' ..."), load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget ("... cannot be combined with 'load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget' ..."), or target.truncateBeforeLoad ("... cannot be combined with 'target.truncateBeforeLoad' ..."). Run time (UpsertGenerator.cs): "ReloadColumn '<value>' is not among the data columns." when the mapped value does not match a bulk-copied target column, plus the mirrored SCD2/DataSetColumn guards. The YAML value is trimmed and blank-normalized to null at load time.

keys.appliesWhen: a keyed flow (load.keyColumns or matchKeys.keyColumns non-empty)
keys.description: Omits the INSERT branch of the keyed upsert: only existing matched rows are updated, new keys are never appended. Consumed as UpsertOptions.SkipInsert (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:908), gating the INSERT statement in UpsertGenerator.GenerateStatements ('if (!options.SkipInsert)', UpsertGenerator.cs:218). Ignored entirely on a keyless flow: BuildInsertAll (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:940-952) always inserts every staged row regardless of this flag. Ignored when versioning.scd2 is enabled (its insert-new-version statement always runs; SkipInsert does not apply, per the UpsertOptions doc comment at UpsertGenerator.cs:95).

keys.appliesWhen: a keyed flow (load.keyColumns or matchKeys.keyColumns non-empty)
keys.description: Omits the UPDATE branch of the keyed upsert: matched rows are never rewritten, only new keys are inserted. Consumed as UpsertOptions.SkipUpdate (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:907), gating the UPDATE statement in UpsertGenerator.GenerateStatements ('if (!options.SkipUpdate && nonKey.Count > 0)', UpsertGenerator.cs:192) and the equivalent branch inside the dataset-partitioned loop script. The UPDATE branch is also naturally skipped whenever every data column is a key column, independent of this flag. Ignored entirely on a keyless flow, which has no update branch at all, and ignored when versioning.scd2 is enabled, whose close/insert statements do not consult SkipUpdate (UpsertOptions doc comment, UpsertGenerator.cs:95).

Accepted and stored verbatim on IngestionLoadPolicy.StreamData (IngestionPolicies.cs:56-58, whose doc comment states 'When false the engine buffers in memory and writes on Threads parallel writers'), but not read anywhere in IngestionFlowRunner: every bulk-copy path (BulkCopyAsync, BulkCopyInitLoadAsync, StreamSelectToStagingAsync; IngestionFlowRunner.cs:954-1042) always streams the source SqlDataReader directly into a single SqlBulkCopy regardless of this flag's value, and the buffered/parallel-writer alternative the model's doc comment describes is not implemented in this runner (confirmed by a solution-wide search: '.StreamData' is only ever written, never read, outside the YAML DTO, the mapped policy record, and the legacy/full-mode row equivalents). Setting it to false only changes what is recorded on the mapped IngestionLoadPolicy, with no observable effect on how a YAML-loaded flow actually runs.

keys.default: null (unset); the one consumer treats null the same as 1 (sequential)
keys.appliesWhen: initLoad.enabled is true (the InitLoad backfill's segment fan-out); unused otherwise
keys.description: Parallel reader/writer count. Consumed only by the InitLoad backfill path: BulkCopyInitLoadAsync computes 'var maxDegree = Math.Max(1, load.Threads ?? 1);' (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:984) and fans its per-segment bulk copies out across a SemaphoreSlim gate of that size; the normal (non-InitLoad) incremental/full read always uses a single connection with no concurrency, so this setting has no effect outside initLoad.enabled: true. Also recorded verbatim on the run-log record for observability (IngestionRunRecord.Threads, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:1219). At YAML load time only a strictly positive value survives: 'Threads = y.Threads is > 0 ? y.Threads : null' (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:281), so 0 or a negative value is silently normalized to null (the same 'engine default' outcome as leaving it unset).

keys.appliesWhen: the flow declares an incremental watermark (incremental.columns or incremental.dateColumn) and the source is a SQL Server connection
keys.description: After a SUCCESSFUL load, truncates the upstream landing ('pre') table that feeds this flow's source, but only once the target has consolidated it: step 8c reads MAX(watermark) from the landing table on the source connection and MAX(watermark) from the target on the target connection, and issues 'TRUNCATE TABLE ...' on the landing table only when the target mark is >= the landing mark; the target-side MAX is scoped by source.incrementalClause when declared, so on a shared target another flow's fresher load cannot fake the catch-up (IngestionFlowRunner.cs, step 8c). The watermark is the first incremental.columns entry, else incremental.dateColumn (ConsolidationWatermarkColumn, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:1283-1285); it must exist under the same name on both sides (the clean, un-renamed FileDate_DW system column and its siblings do). The landing table is the source object with a leading 'v_' stripped (LandingTableOf, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:1290-1293), matching the chained landing pattern 'file -> [pre].[<Table>] -> view [pre].[v<Table>] -> target'; a source that is already a base table is truncated as-is. Designed as the safe replacement for an unconditional truncate: a FAILED run never reaches step 8c (it is on the success path, after the load commits), an empty landing table is a no-op, and a target that has not caught up leaves the landing rows in place so nothing un-consolidated is lost. Independent of the staging lifecycle (load.keepStagingTable / load.truncateStagingOnCompletion), which governs the flow's canonical staging table, not the landing table.
keys.validation: Run start (before any data work, so a misconfigured flow fails immediately rather than after a committed load): "load.truncateSourceWhenConsolidated requires an incremental watermark (incremental.columns or incremental.dateColumn) ..." (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:242-247, when the flag is set but no watermark column resolves) and "load.truncateSourceWhenConsolidated is supported only for SQL Server sources ..." (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:250-254, when the resolved source is not DataSourceKind.MSSQL).

keys.appliesWhen: load.keepStagingTable is true
keys.description: When the staging table is kept after a successful run (load.keepStagingTable: true), truncates it instead of leaving its rows, so the kept table carries structure without the run's data (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:542-548: 'TRUNCATE TABLE ...' when true, otherwise an info log that it was kept with its data). Has no effect when load.keepStagingTable is false: the default branch drops the table outright, which already discards the data, so this flag never fires there.

keys.default: { action: tag, keyColumns: [], thresholdPercent: 20, ignoreDeletedRowsAfterMonths: null, dateColumn: null, sourceFilter: null, targetFilter: null }
keys.appliesWhen: load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true (otherwise parsed and stored but the pass never runs)
keys.description: Optional block configuring the deleted-row detection (key-match) pass: the tag-vs-delete action, the threshold guard, the age-based ignore window, and the key/filter overrides. Binds to IngestionMatchKeysYaml and is mapped by YamlIngestionFlowLoader.MapMatchKeys to SqlFlow.Core.Ingestion.MatchKeyPolicy (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:288-326); absent and present-but-empty both produce the same defaults. The block only takes runtime effect when load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:463); its default Tag action still influences the systemColumns.deletedDate auto-enable at load time even with no explicit matchKeys.action, whenever load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is set (see load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget).

keys.appliesWhen: load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true
keys.description: What to do with a target row whose key vanished from the source: 'tag' soft-deletes by stamping DeletedDate_DW (and RowStatus_DW 'D' when systemColumns.rowStatus is on), leaving the row in place; 'delete' hard-deletes the row. Consumed by MatchKeyGenerator.Generate to choose between the UPDATE-stamp statement and the DELETE statement (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:99-120). Tag mode (whether authored explicitly or left at its default) also drives two other behaviors: at YAML load time, if load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is also true, systemColumns.deletedDate is force-enabled to true regardless of what the YAML said (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:173-176); and at run time, only Tag mode reconciles resurrections, where a previously tagged row whose key reappears in the source is un-tagged (DeletedDate_DW cleared, RowStatus_DW reset to 'U') independent of the threshold guard (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:124-141). Delete mode ignores matchKeys.ignoreDeletedRowsAfterMonths entirely: the age-window predicate is only built in the Tag branch (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:104-110).
keys.validation: "'<source>': 'matchKeys.action' must be 'tag' or 'delete', got '<value>'." (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:299-300), matched by trimming and uppercasing the raw value with no dash/underscore stripping (there being no multi-word spelling to strip); null/absent defaults to Tag without erroring.

keys.default: null; at run time (non-YAML flows only) falls back to incremental.dateColumn
keys.appliesWhen: matchKeys.ignoreDeletedRowsAfterMonths is set
keys.description: The target date column bounding the ignore-after-months window (see matchKeys.ignoreDeletedRowsAfterMonths). Only read at run time when that setting is present: IngestionFlowRunner.RunMatchKeysAsync resolves 'policy.DateColumn ?? flow.Incremental.DateColumn' and maps the chosen name to its bulk-copied target spelling via the source-to-target column map (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:682-685); for a YAML-loaded flow the incremental.dateColumn fallback is never actually exercised, because the loader's load-time validation (see matchKeys.ignoreDeletedRowsAfterMonths) already guarantees this field is set whenever it would be needed.
keys.validation: The name is resolved through the same MapName helper used for key columns, so a value naming an ignored or virtual column (one not among the bulk-copied target columns) fails with "Key column '<name>' is not a bulk-copied target column (is it in IgnoreColumns or a virtual column?)." (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:1157-1161); the generic message text is reused here even though this is a date column, not a business key.

keys.default: null (no age window: the tag action applies to every candidate row regardless of age)
keys.appliesWhen: matchKeys.action resolves to tag; silently ignored in delete mode
keys.description: In Tag mode, restricts the tag action to target rows whose matchKeys.dateColumn value is within this many months of now: the generated candidate predicate adds 'AND trg.[dateColumn] >= DATEADD(MONTH, -{months}, SYSUTCDATETIME())' (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:107-110), so older rows are left untouched (neither tagged nor counted as candidates). Ignored in Delete mode: the Delete branch never builds this predicate at all (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:99-103), so setting this alongside matchKeys.action: delete has no effect and raises no error.
keys.validation: "'<source>': 'matchKeys.ignoreDeletedRowsAfterMonths' requires 'matchKeys.dateColumn'." (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:312-313, load time, whenever this is set and matchKeys.dateColumn is blank, checked before Tag/Delete mode is even known, and regardless of load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget). Two further run-time checks exist for non-YAML-built flows, otherwise unreachable via YAML because the load-time check already guarantees a dateColumn: MatchKeyGenerator.Generate's "IgnoreDeletedRowsAfterMonths requires a date column." (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:89) and IngestionFlowRunner.RunMatchKeysAsync's "matchKeys.ignoreDeletedRowsAfterMonths requires matchKeys.dateColumn (or an incremental dateColumn)." (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:682-684), the latter of which would otherwise fall back to flow.Incremental.DateColumn.

keys.appliesWhen: load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true (otherwise parsed and stored but never read: the check is 'flow.Load.MatchKeysInSourceAndTarget && flow.MatchKeys.KeyColumns.Count > 0', and C#'s && short-circuits, so the property is never even accessed when the flag is false)
keys.description: Overrides load.keyColumns for the whole flow, not just the delete-detection comparison, whenever load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true and this list is non-empty: EffectiveKeyColumns(flow) prefers matchKeys.keyColumns over load.keyColumns in that case (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:817-820), and that effective key set is what the keyed upsert, the schema-evolution critical-mismatch gate, and the canonical/SCD2 index planning all use (see load.keyColumns for the exact consumers and citations), so setting this also changes the business key the upsert matches on, not only which rows the key-match pass considers deleted. When load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is false, this list is parsed and stored but has no effect anywhere.
keys.validation: The same downstream checks as load.keyColumns apply to the resolved effective list: "Key column '<key>' is not among the data columns." (UpsertGenerator.cs:143) and "Key column '<source>' is not a bulk-copied target column (is it in IgnoreColumns or a virtual column?)." (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:1157-1161, for canonical/SCD2 index name-mapping).

keys.appliesWhen: load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true
keys.description: A predicate, raw-append contract (authored with its own leading ' AND '), bounding the SOURCE rows read to build the 'still present' key set for the delete-detection pass. IngestionFlowRunner.RunMatchKeysAsync resolves it as 'policy.SourceFilter, else flow.Source.Filter' (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:704, trimmed at the point of use), so an unset matchKeys.sourceFilter reuses the flow's own source.filter, meaning rows the load itself never reads are, by default, not wrongly treated as deleted. The key scan this bounds is a fresh 'SELECT DISTINCT ...' over the full source (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:706-710) and deliberately never applies the incremental window, so a row outside the current run's incremental read is still correctly recognized as present in the source.

keys.default: null (no restriction on the candidate/action/resurrect statements; the total-row count is never restricted by this field regardless of its value)
keys.appliesWhen: load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true
keys.description: CORRECTED: A predicate, raw-append contract (authored with its own leading ' AND '), bounding which TARGET rows the key-match pass may count as a candidate or act on. MatchKeyGenerator.Generate appends the trimmed filter (captured once at MatchKeyGenerator.cs:95) to three places: the candidate-count query (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:148), the tag/delete action statement (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:102 for Delete mode, :119 for Tag mode), and, in Tag mode only, the resurrect statement (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:139). It is NOT applied to the target's TOTAL-row count, which is the threshold's denominator: 'SELECT @Total = COUNT_BIG(*) FROM {trg};' (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:147) counts the whole target table unconditionally, with no targetFilter, no candidatePredicates, and not even a 'trg' alias. Practical consequence: when targetFilter narrows the pass to a subset of the target, the reported/enforced breach percentage (@Candidates * 100.0 / @Total) is candidates-within-the-filtered-subset divided by the WHOLE unfiltered target's row count, not the filtered subset's size, so a targetFilter that scopes to a small slice of a large table makes even a total wipeout of that slice register as a small percentage and can silently slip under matchKeys.thresholdPercent.

keys.appliesWhen: load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true
keys.description: Skips the tag/delete action (and reports it) when more than this percentage of the target would be affected. MatchKeyGenerator's generated script computes '@Candidates * 100.0 / @Total > {threshold}' and, when breached, sets @Breached and skips the action statement entirely while still reporting @Total/@Candidates (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:146-158). The comparison is only evaluated when the target has at least one row (@Total > 0), so an empty target can never breach. Resurrection (un-tagging a reappeared key) is independent of this threshold and always runs when applicable. A breach is surfaced as a warning-level log line by IngestionFlowRunner.RunMatchKeysAsync, not a run failure (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:729-736).
keys.validation: "'<source>': 'matchKeys.thresholdPercent' must be 0 to 100, got <value>." (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:306-307, load time). The same range is re-checked defensively at run time by MatchKeyGenerator.Generate: "ActionThresholdPercent must be 0 to 100, got {value}." (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:79), reachable only from a flow assembled outside the YAML loader.

keys.default: null (unset); FlowId is then 0 and SysAlias is null
keys.description: The flow's display name. Unlike the file flow (where 'name' is required), it is optional for an ing document. When non-blank it is trimmed (`y.Name.Trim()`, YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:100) and becomes IngestionFlow.SysAlias verbatim (legacy flw.Ingestion.SysAlias), and it seeds IngestionFlow.FlowId via YamlDocumentParts.StableFlowId: the trimmed name is hashed into the same name-based RFC4122 v5 GUID the file flow uses (FlowIdentity.FromName, confirmed a SHA-1 name-based v5 UUID over a fixed namespace constant), and BitConverter.ToInt32 of the GUID's first four bytes, masked with 0x7FFFFFFF (clearing the sign bit), yields a stable non-negative int32 -- because unlike the file flow's GUID identity, the legacy flw.Ingestion.FlowID column (and this model's FlowId) is a plain int. A blank or missing name yields SysAlias = null and FlowId = 0 (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:180-181). FlowId is not just informational: IngestionFlowRunner names the flow's canonical staging table `[raw].[<targetSchema>_<targetTable>_<FlowId>]` and the match-key table `[raw].[mkey_<targetSchema>_<targetTable>_<FlowId>]` (CanonicalWorkTableName, IngestionFlowRunner.cs), and stamps FlowId on the run-log record (BuildRunRecord, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:1204). SysAlias, when set, appears in the run-start log line and otherwise falls back to the target table name there (`flow.SysAlias ?? flow.Target.Table.Name`, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:208), and is also stamped on the run-log record (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:1208).

The flow's execution mode, read at the document envelope (YamlDocumentLoader's probe, FlowDocument.Mode) and projected to the catalog pipeline row. 'auto' (the default) runs on schedule fires and in batch/node group runs; 'manual' reserves a working flow for direct triggers; 'disabled' deactivates a retired one (a retired source, a run-once replay) with the same exclusions and a visible 'disabled' badge. A node-scoped run can opt into includeAll ('find all') to replay non-auto descendants deliberately, and naming a flow directly always runs it.

Applied unconditionally by IngestionSchemaBuilder.Build (used for both the staging and target desired schemas), so it is not gated by schema.sync.

keys.description: Gates whether the target table's schema is created or evolved on this run. When true (the default), IngestionFlowRunner calls schemaSync.EvolveAsync against the target with the desired column list, creating the table if it is missing or ALTER-adding new source columns (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:334-355); when false, that call is skipped entirely, so a first run against a non-existent target never creates it (the subsequent load statements would then fail against a table SQL Server cannot find) and new source columns are never propagated onto an existing target. Because targetCreated is only ever set true inside this same gate, a false sync also skips the automatic canonical-index creation and desired-index application that otherwise follow a table-creating run. Only the TARGET-side evolution is gated: the canonical staging table is always created (schemaSync.EvolveAsync runs unconditionally for it, with allowTableRewrite hardcoded false, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:266), and column-name cleanup (cleanColumnNames) and unicode conversion (convertUnicodeToNonUnicode) run unconditionally inside IngestionSchemaBuilder.Build, whose single result feeds both the staging and target passes.

The source's three-part relational object name, Database.Schema.Table (or Database.Table for MySQL-style sources; see below). Resolved by YamlIngestionFlowLoader.ParseObject (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:242-261), shared verbatim between source and target -- only the 'section' label ('source' or 'target') differs. Resolution order: 'object' wins over the 'table' alias (see source.table); whichever is non-blank is then, when it contains no '[' at all, checked for the MySQL two-part convention: a plain (unbracketed) two-segment name 'X.Y' (both segments non-empty after `Split('.', StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries)`) is expanded to 'X.X.Y', treating the database part as also the schema (natural for MySQL, which has no separate schema level). The (possibly-expanded) string is then parsed by RelationalObject.Parse (src/SqlFlow.Core/Ingestion/RelationalObject.cs:20-48): it splits on '.' while respecting [bracketed] identifiers (IngestionText.SplitRespectingBrackets, confirmed bracket-depth-aware with an inner ']' escaped as ']]'), trims and unbrackets each segment (IngestionText.Unbracket), and takes the RIGHTMOST three segments as Database/Schema/Name -- so a name with more than three dotted segments (for example a stray leading server part) silently drops everything left of the third-from-last segment rather than failing. The result becomes IngestionSource.Table (a RelationalObject), whose QualifiedName renders back out as '[Database].[Schema].[Name]' with any ']' doubled inside identifiers.

(YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:244-247). When the resolved name (after any two-part expansion) has fewer than three dot-separated segments: "<source>: 'source.object': Object name '<name>' must be a three-part [Database].[Schema].[Object] name; found <n> part(s)." (RelationalObject.cs:34-35, rewrapped by YamlDocumentParts.ParseQualifiedObject at YamlDocumentParts.cs:181-191, which always labels the field 'source.object' even when the raw value came from the 'table' alias). When the database, schema, or object segment is empty after trimming (e.g. 'Db..Table'): "<source>: 'source.object': Object name '<name>' has an empty database, schema, or object part." (RelationalObject.cs:42-44).

keys.description: Injects a nullable datetime2(3) DeletedDate_DW column onto the target (IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:93), the soft-delete stamp the key-match pass's Tag action writes: SYSUTCDATETIME() when a row's key vanishes from the source, cleared back to NULL if the key later reappears (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:112,128). Consumed as MatchKeyScriptOptions.DeletedDateColumn ('DeletedDate_DW' when true, else null, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:721). Cross-cutting load-time override: when load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true and matchKeys.action resolves to Tag (its default), YamlIngestionFlowLoader force-enables this to true regardless of the authored value; an explicit 'deletedDate: false' is silently overridden (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:173-176, pinned by test YamlIngestionMatchKeysTests.TagMode_AutoEnableOverridesExplicitFalseOnDeletedDate). The run-time requirement below is therefore only reachable for a flow assembled outside the YAML loader, where matchKeysInSourceAndTarget and Tag mode are set without this column enabled.
keys.validation: "Tag mode requires the DeletedDate column (enable the DeletedDate_DW system column)." (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:82-85, when matchKeys.action is Tag and this is false) and, equivalently, "MatchKeys Tag mode soft-deletes by stamping DeletedDate_DW; enable the DeletedDate_DW system column." (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:673-677, the runner's own pre-check before generating the script).

keys.description: CORRECTED: Injects a nullable datetime2(3) InsertedDate_DW column onto the target (IngestionSchemaBuilder.AddSystemColumns, IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:91). On a keyed flow it is stamped SYSUTCDATETIME() on every INSERT (UpsertGenerator.cs:222-226) and, on the UPDATE branch, back-filled with SYSUTCDATETIME() only for a matched row whose existing value is NULL (a row that predates the column); otherwise its existing value is preserved ('CASE WHEN trg.[...] IS NULL THEN SYSUTCDATETIME() ELSE trg.[...] END', UpsertGenerator.cs:568-574, legacy parity). On a KEYLESS flow (insert-all), it is the ONLY system column ever stamped: BuildInsertAll only checks 'system.InsertedDate' and stamps SYSUTCDATETIME() on insert; it does not accept or stamp UpdatedDate_DW or RowStatus_DW at all, even when those are enabled (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:940-952). When versioning.scd2 is enabled, the SCD2 insert-new-version statement stamps it with the shared as-of instant on every brand-new/changed version it inserts (UpsertGenerator.cs:338-342). Separately, the SCD2 backfill statement (which runs first, and touches only PRE-EXISTING TARGET rows whose period columns are still NULL, via 'UPDATE trg SET ... FROM {trg} AS trg WHERE trg.[ValidTo] IS NULL', with no staging/source ('src') reference anywhere in that statement, UpsertGenerator.cs:297-303) uses that same target row's own existing InsertedDate_DW value, when present, as its inferred ValidFrom, falling back to the 1900-01-01 epoch sentinel otherwise (UpsertGenerator.cs:294-296); this is the pre-existing TARGET row's own value, not a 'source row's' value.

keys.appliesWhen: a keyed flow (never populated on a keyless flow even when enabled)
keys.description: Injects a nullable char(1) RowStatus_DW column onto the target (IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:94), a per-row action code the engine stamps: 'I' on insert and 'U' on update (UpsertGenerator's insert branch and UpdateSetClauses, UpsertGenerator.cs:231,576-578); 'D' when the key-match pass tags a row deleted and 'U' again when it resurrects a previously tagged row (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:115,131); and, when versioning.scd2 is enabled, 'U' when an SCD2 version is closed and 'I' when its replacement version is inserted (UpsertGenerator.cs:316-318,344-347). Consumed as UpsertOptions.RowStatusColumn / MatchKeyScriptOptions.RowStatusColumn ('RowStatus_DW' when true, else null). Like systemColumns.updatedDate, only meaningfully stamped on a KEYED flow; a keyless flow's insert-all statement never references RowStatus_DW, so on a keyless flow the column is added to the schema when enabled but is never populated.

keys.appliesWhen: a keyed flow (never populated on a keyless flow even when enabled)
keys.description: Injects a nullable datetime2(3) UpdatedDate_DW column onto the target (IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:92). Stamped SYSUTCDATETIME() only on the keyed upsert's UPDATE branch (UpsertGenerator.UpdateSetClauses, UpsertGenerator.cs:563-565) and, when versioning.scd2 is enabled, on the SCD2 close-of-current-version statement (UpsertGenerator.cs:308-312). It is never set on insert, so a freshly inserted row's UpdatedDate_DW stays NULL until it is later updated. A keyless flow's insert-all statement (BuildInsertAll, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:940-952) never references UpdatedDate_DW at all, so on a keyless flow the column is still added to the schema when enabled but is never populated by any statement the engine generates.

The target endpoint: where the flow writes. Binds to the same IngestionEndpointYaml DTO as 'source' and maps to the required IngestionTarget on IngestionFlow.Target. As with 'source', this unit covers this block's presence/requiredness, the 'object'/'table' three-part-name resolution, 'identityColumn', 'truncateBeforeLoad', and the canonical-index-related 'columnStoreIndex' flag. Connection routing is documented in the connections unit -- the resolved connection must additionally be SQL Server (mssql or azdb), enforced by the shared YamlDocumentParts.RequireSqlServerConnection helper (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:95), because staging, schema evolution, and the upsert are all T-SQL; that check and its message are out of this unit's scope. 'desiredIndexes' is explicitly excluded from this unit (documented in the shared unit) and is likewise out of scope here.
keys.validation: Missing block throws FlowValidationException "<source>: 'target' is required." (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:88).

keys.description: Requests a clustered columnstore index on the target, bound to IngestionTarget.ColumnStoreIndex (legacy 'ColumnStoreIndexOnTrg'). This is the main entry point into canonical index behavior: on the run that CREATEs the target table (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:359, gated by `if (targetCreated)`, itself only reachable when schema sync is enabled), IngestionFlowRunner calls CanonicalIndexPlanner.Plan (CanonicalIndexPlanner.cs:17-68), which emits, over the freshly-created (still-empty) table, all of the following as idempotent `IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.indexes ...) CREATE ...` statements with stable, non-hashed names: (1) 'NCI_KeyColumn', a UNIQUE NONCLUSTERED index on the flow's effective key columns (load.keyColumns, overridden by matchKeys.keyColumns when the key-match pass is active -- both out of this unit's scope; confirmed via EffectiveKeyColumns, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:817-820), only when there is at least one key column AND SCD2 is not enabled; (2) 'NCI_DateColumn', a plain NONCLUSTERED index on incremental.dateColumn (out of scope), only when that column is set and maps to a real bulk-copied target column; (3) 'NCI_DataSetColumn' (see source.dataSetColumn); (4) 'NCI_UpdatedDate_DW', a plain NONCLUSTERED index on UpdatedDate_DW, only when the desired schema carries that column (systemColumns.updatedDate, out of scope); and (5), only when THIS flag is true AND the desired schema has no identity primary key (see target.identityColumn), a clustered columnstore index named 'CCSI_' followed by the target table's own name with every character that is not a letter, digit, or underscore stripped (CanonicalIndexPlanner.Sanitize, CanonicalIndexPlanner.cs:61,137-138). A REQUIRED key column that does not resolve to a real bulk-copied target column (for example because it is in source.ignoreColumns or is a virtual column) FAILS THE RUN with SqlFlowException "Key column '<source>' is not a bulk-copied target column (is it in IgnoreColumns or a virtual column?)." (IngestionFlowRunner.MapName, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:1157-1161); the optional date/dataset columns instead silently produce no index when unmappable (MapNameOrNull, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:1165-1166), never failing the run. Separately from this once-at-creation Plan(), whenever versioning.scd2.enabled is true (out of scope), CanonicalIndexPlanner.Scd2KeyIndexStatements runs on EVERY run, not only at creation (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:382-393): it drops any pre-existing 'NCI_KeyColumn' (or any other non-filtered unique nonclustered index whose columns exactly match the key columns) and creates a FILTERED unique index 'NCI_KeyColumn ... WHERE [<currentFlagColumn>] = 1' instead, because under SCD2 the business key is unique only among current rows -- this is how turning SCD2 on for an already-created table migrates its key index. All of the above map column names using SOURCE names as declared on the flow through the bulk-copy name map to the cleaned TARGET names before building any statement.
keys.validation: None on this key itself (a plain YAML bool, coerced by the YamlDotNet deserializer); the run-time key-column-mapping failure described above is triggered by load.keyColumns / matchKeys.keyColumns (out of scope), not by this flag.
keys.appliesWhen: Only takes effect on the run that creates the target table; a no-op on every later run against an already-existing target (there is no retrofit path for canonical indexes).

keys.default: null (unset); no computed identity column is added
keys.description: Name of a computed IDENTITY primary-key column added to the DESIRED TARGET schema only -- never to the canonical staging table, since IngestionFlowRunner always builds the target schema with `IngestionSchemaBuilder.Build(sourceColumns, flow, forStaging: false)` (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:240), and IngestionSchemaBuilder.AddIdentity runs only `if (!forStaging)` (IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:81-84); the staging table's own columns are instead derived directly from the bulk-copied source columns and never carry this column. When blank, AddIdentity is a no-op. When non-blank and no existing desired column already has that name (case-insensitive), AddIdentity appends a new column: SQL type 'int', NOT NULL, Role=Identity, IsIdentity=true, IsPrimaryKey=true (IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:129-146); when a column of that name already exists (for example a same-named source column), AddIdentity silently skips adding it -- the existing column is left exactly as inferred/authored and is NOT retrofitted with identity/primary-key semantics. Only the target-table CREATE path actually renders identity/primary-key SQL: EvolutionDdlGenerator.CreateTableStatement adds a `CONSTRAINT [PK_<table>] PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED (...)` over every column flagged IsPrimaryKey (EvolutionDdlGenerator.cs:79-84), and ColumnDefinition appends ' IDENTITY(1, 1)' to a column flagged IsIdentity (EvolutionDdlGenerator.cs:100); the additive ALTER path used against an already-existing table (ColumnsToAdd) always renders a plain nullable column with neither clause (EvolutionDdlGenerator.cs:52-60). Confirmed (by reading SchemaEvolutionPlanner.cs, one file outside this unit's assigned list) that this ALTER path is genuinely reachable for identityColumn: SchemaEvolutionPlanner.Plan puts any desired column absent from the existing table's columns, including a newly-declared identityColumn, into ColumnsToAdd purely by name lookup (SchemaEvolutionPlanner.cs:34-38), with no special-casing for identity/PK columns. So declaring identityColumn against a target that already exists without it DOES add the column on the next run, just always as a plain nullable column, never retrofitted with identity/primary-key semantics. The column's presence also feeds canonical-index planning: IngestionFlowRunner computes `hasIdentityPrimaryKey: targetSchema.Columns.Any(c => c.IsPrimaryKey)` (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:368) and passes it to CanonicalIndexPlanner.Plan, which suppresses the clustered columnstore index whenever an identity primary key is present, because a clustered columnstore index cannot coexist with a clustered rowstore primary key (see target.columnStoreIndex).
keys.appliesWhen: Meaningfully creates an identity/primary-key column only on the run that CREATEs the target table.

keys.description: The target's three-part relational object name. Identical mechanism to source.object (same ParseObject function, same two-part MySQL expansion, same RelationalObject.Parse rules, same rightmost-three-segments behavior); only the error-message section label differs ('target.object' instead of 'source.object'). See source.object for the full parsing description. The resulting RelationalObject also supplies the canonical staging table's database and name parts (IngestionFlowRunner builds the staging object from flow.Target.Table.Database plus the raw schema and the CanonicalWorkTableName derived from the target's schema, name, and FlowId) and is the table the canonical indexes (see target.columnStoreIndex), the truncate step (see target.truncateBeforeLoad), and the match-key/upsert scripts run against.

Truncates the target table immediately before staging is applied, for full-reload semantics (legacy 'TruncateTrg' column, IngestionFlow.cs:31 comment). Bound via `targetYaml.TruncateBeforeLoad ?? false` (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:199) onto IngestionTarget.TruncateBeforeLoad. When true, IngestionFlowRunner emits and executes `TRUNCATE TABLE [schema].[table];` (two-part, schema-qualified, since the connection is already scoped to the target database) as run step 6 (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:396-402): after staging is filled and the target schema is evolved (and, on a create, after the canonical indexes and any SCD2 key index are applied), but before the keyed upsert / insert-all apply step. Unlike target.columnStoreIndex, target.identityColumn, and source.dataSetColumn (all consequential only on the run that creates the target), this flag is read and acted on EVERY run: any run with truncateBeforeLoad true wipes the table's rows immediately before every load, not just the first. The TRUNCATE statement carries no `IF OBJECT_ID(...) IS NOT NULL`-style guard, unlike the rest of the engine's DDL/DML in this runner (DropStagingAsync's `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS`, the canonical indexes' `IF NOT EXISTS`, EvolutionDdlGenerator's `IF OBJECT_ID(...) IS NULL`); so if `schema.sync` is off and the target has never been created, this statement fails against a nonexistent table. That failure is still caught by RunAsync's outer handler (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:602), so the run ends gracefully as `IngestionRunResult { Success = false }`, but `Error` carries the raw underlying SqlException text (e.g. an 'Invalid object name' message) rather than a curated SqlFlowException/FlowValidationException message the way most anticipated engine failures are reported. Cross-validated at parse time against SCD2 (see validation): 'versioning.scd2.enabled: true' cannot combine with this flag, because SCD2 appends a new dated version per change and a truncate would erase that whole history.
keys.validation: `versioning.scd2.enabled: true` combined with `target.truncateBeforeLoad: true` is rejected at parse time: FlowValidationException "<source>: 'versioning.scd2' cannot be combined with 'target.truncateBeforeLoad'; truncating would erase the dimension history." (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:133-137, only reached when versioning.scd2.enabled is true). No other validation on the key itself (a plain YAML bool). Cross-validated the same way against system-versioned history: 'versioning.temporal.enabled: true' (or the 'versioning.temporalHistory: true' shorthand) cannot combine with this flag, because SQL Server does not allow TRUNCATE TABLE on a system-versioned table at all: FlowValidationException "<source>: 'versioning.temporal' cannot be combined with 'target.truncateBeforeLoad'. ...", repeated at run time by IngestionFlowRunner.EnsureSupportedFeatures for the non-YAML load paths.
keys.appliesWhen: Applies on every run where the flag is true, not gated to the run that creates the target, unlike target.columnStoreIndex / target.identityColumn / source.dataSetColumn. On the very same run that creates the target the TRUNCATE is a harmless no-op against the just-created empty table.

keys.default: { temporal: { enabled: false, historySchema: ver, historyTable: null, validFromColumn: ValidFrom_DW, validToColumn: ValidTo_DW, hiddenPeriodColumns: true, periodPrecision: 7, retentionDays: null }, insertUnknownDimensionRow: false, tokenVersioning: false, tokenRetentionDays: null, scd2: { enabled: false, validFromColumn: ValidFrom_DW, validToColumn: ValidTo_DW, currentFlagColumn: IsCurrent_DW, trackedColumns: [] } }
keys.description: Optional target-history block for a relational ingestion flow (flowType: ing). Binds to IngestionVersioningYaml and is mapped by YamlIngestionFlowLoader.MapVersioning into SqlFlow.Core.Ingestion.VersioningPolicy, carried on IngestionFlow.Versioning through the whole run. It offers two independent, MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE history mechanisms. 'temporal' is SQL Server system-versioned temporal history (legacy trgVersioning): the database itself keeps every superseded row version in a paired history table, so the target is queryable as of any past instant with FOR SYSTEM_TIME, and because the period columns are HIDDEN by default the target's visible column list does not change. 'scd2' is application-managed SCD Type 2 history, keeping versions as ordinary rows inside the target itself. Enabling both is rejected, because each change would be recorded twice. The direct boolean 'temporalHistory' is the legacy shorthand for 'temporal.enabled' (it is the key a ported trgVersioning flow carries) and converges on the same TemporalPolicy, so there is one execution path and two authoring surfaces. Of the remaining direct keys, 'insertUnknownDimensionRow' is rejected when set to true, and 'tokenVersioning'/'tokenRetentionDays' are parsed and stored but read by no engine code. When the 'versioning' key itself is absent, MapVersioning still runs and returns the all-off default policy.
keys.validation: Load time (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.MapVersioning): FlowValidationException "<source>: 'versioning.temporal' and 'versioning.scd2' cannot both be enabled. ... Choose one." Run time, for flows not built via this loader (IngestionFlowRunner.EnsureSupportedFeatures): the same combination, plus 'versioning.temporal' with 'target.truncateBeforeLoad', fail the run with SqlFlowException before any data work.

keys.description: Would insert an unknown-member row for dimension handling (legacy InsertUnknownDimRow). NOT YET IMPLEMENTED: per the model's doc comment, a correct implementation needs a defined sentinel-key convention plus exemption from the match-key delete pass (src/SqlFlow.Core/Ingestion/IngestionPolicies.cs:238-241), so a flow that sets it to true is rejected rather than silently doing nothing. It is rejected twice: at YAML load, so an authored flow never gets further, and again at run time by IngestionFlowRunner.EnsureSupportedFeatures, which guards flows assembled through the other loaders (full-mode control-DB, legacy migration) that do not go through this YAML loader (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Ingestion/IngestionFlowRunner.cs:205, 837-841).

Run time, for flows not built via this loader (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:837-841): SqlFlowException "insertUnknownDimensionRow is not yet implemented. keys.default: { enabled: false, validFromColumn: ValidFrom_DW, validToColumn: ValidTo_DW, currentFlagColumn: IsCurrent_DW, trackedColumns: [] }
keys.description: Application-managed slowly-changing-dimension Type 2 (period-based) target history: the engine keeps a validity period per business-key row instead of overwriting it, so unlike 'versioning.temporal' (whose versions live in a separate, database-maintained history table reached through FOR SYSTEM_TIME) its versions are ordinary rows in the target that any SQL or BI tool can join; both can be turned on for an already-created, already-populated target (the period columns are added through ordinary schema evolution, and every pre-existing row is backfilled as the current version the first time the flow runs with it on). Binds to IngestionScd2Yaml and is mapped, with validation, by YamlIngestionFlowLoader.MapScd2 into SqlFlow.Core.Ingestion.Scd2Policy. Consumed by three collaborators once 'enabled' is true: IngestionSchemaBuilder.AddScd2Columns adds the three period columns to the target's desired schema, UpsertGenerator.GenerateScd2Statements replaces the plain two-step upsert with a backfill, close, and insert load, and CanonicalIndexPlanner turns the business-key index into a filtered unique index. When the whole 'scd2' key is absent, MapScd2 returns the disabled default without running the distinct-name check below, since it never computes candidate names to check. The legacy/full-mode row mapper (src/SqlFlow.Core/Ingestion/Legacy/IngestionFlowMapper.cs:136-142) never sets this sub-object at all, so today 'versioning.scd2' is reachable only by authoring the YAML flowType: ing document; a full-mode or legacy-sourced flow always gets the disabled Scd2Policy default.
keys.validation: The three period-column names below (each independently defaulted first) must be pairwise distinct, case-insensitively, whenever the 'scd2' block itself is present, regardless of 'enabled' (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:437-448): FlowValidationException "<source>: 'versioning.scd2' validFromColumn, validToColumn, and currentFlagColumn must be three distinct names (got '<validFrom>', '<validTo>', '<current>')." Additionally, 'versioning.scd2.enabled: true' cannot combine with 'versioning.temporal.enabled: true' (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.MapVersioning): two history mechanisms on one table would record every change twice.

keys.description: The current-row indicator column: 1 for the live version of a key, 0 for an expired one. When 'versioning.scd2.enabled' is true, IngestionSchemaBuilder.AddScd2Columns adds it to the target's desired schema (not the staging table, which the production runner builds through a separate, simpler column projection) as a nullable 'bit' system-role column, skipping the add if a same-named column already exists (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:100-109, AddComputed at 148-163). At run time UpsertGenerator.GenerateScd2Statements sets it to 1 on backfilled rows and newly-inserted current versions, clears it to 0 when closing a changed current row, and uses 'trg.[column] = 1' as the anti-join condition that finds keys needing a new current version (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/UpsertGenerator.cs:301, 308, 321-329, 355-362). It is also the filter predicate of the migrated business-key index: on every run where scd2 is enabled, not only the run that creates the target, IngestionFlowRunner calls CanonicalIndexPlanner.Scd2KeyIndexStatements, which drops a same-named 'NCI_KeyColumn' that is not already a filtered unique index, drops any other non-filtered unique nonclustered index whose columns are exactly the business key, and creates 'CREATE UNIQUE NONCLUSTERED INDEX [NCI_KeyColumn] ON <target> (<keyColumns>) WHERE [<currentFlagColumn>] = 1' (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Ingestion/CanonicalIndexPlanner.cs:70-126, called from src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Ingestion/IngestionFlowRunner.cs:382-393). On the run that creates the target, CanonicalIndexPlanner.Plan also uses 'versioning.scd2.enabled' itself (not this column) to suppress the plain, non-filtered unique 'NCI_KeyColumn' it would otherwise emit (CanonicalIndexPlanner.cs:36-40).
keys.appliesWhen: versioning.scd2.enabled: true for any schema or SQL effect; the value is still parsed and validated for distinctness even when enabled is false or the key is absent from an otherwise-present scd2 block
keys.validation: Blank or whitespace falls back to the default (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:439, NullIfBlank). Together with validFromColumn and validToColumn it must be pairwise distinct: FlowValidationException "<source>: 'versioning.scd2' validFromColumn, validToColumn, and currentFlagColumn must be three distinct names (got '<validFrom>', '<validTo>', '<current>')." (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:437-448).

keys.description: Turns on the SCD2 load path. Off (the default), a keyed flow always applies through the plain two-step upsert. On, UpsertGenerator.GenerateStatements dispatches to GenerateScd2Statements instead (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/UpsertGenerator.cs:179-182), and 'load.skipUpdateExisting'/'load.skipInsertNew' are not consulted at all, because the SCD2 statement set replaces both plain branches entirely, per the UpsertOptions.Scd2Enabled doc comment (UpsertGenerator.cs:93-96); 'load.batchUpsert' and 'load.batchUpsertRowCount' (BatchToAvoidLockEscalation) are likewise never applied to the SCD2 statements, only to the plain and dataset-partitioned-loop paths, since GenerateStatements returns from the SCD2 branch before reaching that logic. The business key used by the SCD2 statements, and by the canonical or filtered index, is the flow's effective key columns (load.keyColumns, overridden by matchKeys.keyColumns when load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is also on), computed by IngestionFlowRunner.EffectiveKeyColumns (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:817-820, 903-926); this can differ from the plain 'load.keyColumns' count that the load-time validation below inspects. On the run that creates the target, CanonicalIndexPlanner.Plan suppresses the plain unique 'NCI_KeyColumn' index when this flag is on (CanonicalIndexPlanner.cs:36-40); on every run where it is on, IngestionFlowRunner additionally reconciles the key index to the SCD2 filtered-unique form via CanonicalIndexPlanner.Scd2KeyIndexStatements (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:382-393), which is how enabling SCD2 on a pre-existing table migrates its key index before the load can insert a second version of a key.

Not checked at YAML load time, but enforced at run time when the flow also sets 'load.dataSetColumn' (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/UpsertGenerator.cs:152-157, reached from IngestionFlowRunner.BuildLoadStatements when the flow runs): SqlFlowException "A dataset-column load (DataSetColumn) cannot be combined with SCD2 versioning."

keys.description: SOURCE column names whose change opens a new dimension version; a change in any other column leaves the current row untouched. IngestionFlowRunner maps each entry to its cleaned TARGET name through the same source-to-target name map used for 'change.ignoreColumnsInHash', silently dropping any entry that is not a real bulk-copied column (for example one named in source.ignoreColumns, or a virtual column), before passing the mapped list to UpsertGenerator as Scd2TrackedColumns (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Ingestion/IngestionFlowRunner.cs:893-896, 921). Inside UpsertGenerator.GenerateScd2Statements, a non-empty mapped list is intersected with the target's non-key data columns; an empty list instead falls back to every column already eligible for the plain change-detection checksum (every non-key column whose type supports HASHBYTES/CONCAT and that is not in change.ignoreColumnsInHash). Either way, columns excluded from the checksum are removed from the tracked set, and if nothing remains comparable the close statement is skipped entirely, so only brand-new keys get inserted and no existing current row is ever closed (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/UpsertGenerator.cs:282-289, 306-329).
keys.appliesWhen: versioning.scd2.enabled: true; when false the list is still parsed but IngestionFlowRunner never reads it (scd2Tracked is forced to an empty list, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:894-896)

keys.description: One SOURCE column name to track for SCD2 change detection. A blank or whitespace-only entry is filtered out while mapping the YAML list (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:456, NullIfBlank inside MapScd2); a non-blank entry that does not resolve to a bulk-copied target column, because it names an ignored or virtual column, is filtered out at run time instead of erroring (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:895, MapNameOrNull). Neither case raises a validation error; see 'versioning.scd2.trackedColumns' for how the resulting set is used.

The period-start column name. When 'versioning.scd2.enabled' is true, IngestionSchemaBuilder.AddScd2Columns adds it to the target's desired schema as a nullable 'datetime2(3)' system-role column, skipping the add if a same-named column already exists (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:100-109, AddComputed at 148-163); being nullable is what lets the ALTER TABLE ADD succeed on an already-populated target. Final column position is rank-based, not add-order-based: IngestionSchemaBuilder.Order buckets every column into Rank 0 (name starts with 'PK'), Rank 1 (ends with 'PK'), Rank 2 (ordinary), or Rank 3 (ends with '_DW'), sorts by rank first, and only breaks ties within the same rank by the column's original build-order index. A name (default or overridden) ending in '_DW' falls into Rank 3, so it sorts after every ordinary (Rank 2) column, including the real source/virtual data columns. A custom name that does NOT end in '_DW' instead falls into Rank 2, the same rank as an ordinary source column, so it sorts BEFORE all '_DW' columns (not after them); within that Rank-2 group it lands after the real source/virtual columns, because AddScd2Columns appends it to the internal column list after they were added (IngestionSchemaBuilder.Order and Rank, IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:168-192). At run time UpsertGenerator.GenerateScd2Statements both reads and writes it: the backfill statement sets it, for any target row whose period is still NULL, to the existing value if present, else InsertedDate_DW when that system column is on, else the epoch '1900-01-01 00:00:00.000'; the insert statement sets it to the run's single as-of instant (captured once per run so a closed row's ValidTo equals the new row's ValidFrom exactly) for every new current version (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/UpsertGenerator.cs:278, 293-303, 333-342).

keys.validation: Blank or whitespace falls back to the default (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:437, NullIfBlank). Together with validToColumn and currentFlagColumn it must be pairwise distinct: FlowValidationException "<source>: 'versioning.scd2' validFromColumn, validToColumn, and currentFlagColumn must be three distinct names (got '<validFrom>', '<validTo>', '<current>')." (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:437-448).

keys.description: The period-end column name; the current version of a key holds the open-ended sentinel '9999-12-31 23:59:59.999' (the maximum datetime2(3) value, UpsertGenerator.Scd2OpenSentinel, src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/UpsertGenerator.cs:260), so every point-in-time query over the dimension is a uniform half-open ValidFrom-to-ValidTo range with no NULL special case. Added to the target's desired schema the same way as validFromColumn: a nullable 'datetime2(3)' system-role column, skipped if already present (IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:100-109); the same Rank-based column-ordering rule applies (see 'versioning.scd2.validFromColumn'). At run time: the backfill statement stamps it with the open sentinel for any row whose period is NULL; the close statement stamps it with the run's as-of instant on a current row (flag equal to 1) whose tracked attributes changed from the staged row; the insert statement stamps it with the open sentinel on every new current version (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/UpsertGenerator.cs:293-303, 305-329, 333-342).

keys.description: The legacy trgVersioning shorthand: identical to setting 'versioning.temporal.enabled' to the same value, with every other temporal setting left at its default. Both surfaces are OR-ed together by YamlIngestionFlowLoader.MapTemporal into the single TemporalPolicy the engine reads, so a ported legacy flow needs nothing else. The legacy control-DB mapper (IngestionFlowMapper.FromLegacy) maps flw.Ingestion.trgVersioning onto the same policy, additionally pinning periodPrecision to 0 because that is what flw.GetVersioningScript emitted. See 'versioning.temporal' for what the engine does with it.

'temporalHistory' is the shorthand for 'temporal.enabled'; set one of them." An absent shorthand is not a contradiction. Every other guard is the one documented on 'versioning.temporal'.

keys.description: SQL Server system-versioned temporal history for the target (legacy trgVersioning, legacy flw.GetVersioningScript). SQL Server keeps every superseded version of a row in a paired history table that it maintains itself, so an UPDATE or DELETE on the target is never lossy and the table is queryable as of any past instant with FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF / ALL. Planned from the LIVE target state by src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/TemporalTablePlanner.cs and applied as run step 11, after schema evolution and the create-time indexes: SQL Server refuses to version a table with no PRIMARY KEY (which the create step supplies), and adding the SYSTEM_TIME period last keeps the period columns out of the schema the evolution planner diffs. Four outcomes depending on that live state: no period -> add the period then enable; period present but versioning off (a manual SET SYSTEM_VERSIONING = OFF leaves the period behind, as does a run interrupted between the two statements) -> only enable; already versioned into the declared history table -> nothing, unless retentionDays differs, which is re-applied; already versioned into a DIFFERENT history table -> the run fails, because re-pointing would orphan the history already recorded. Unlike the legacy engine, which applied versioning only in its create-a-new-table branch, this can be turned on for a target that already exists and already holds rows: the existing rows' ROW START is stamped one second in the past so no row's period is empty and every row stays visible to FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF. Turning the flag back OFF never un-versions the table and never drops history; that is an explicit operator action, not a side effect of an edited YAML. Ordinary dynamic schema evolution keeps working on a versioned target: SQL Server supports ADD, ALTER and DROP COLUMN while versioning is on and propagates each change to the history table, so the engine never toggles versioning off to fit a schema change through (which would open a window where changes go unrecorded). The period columns are GENERATED ALWAYS, so the engine excludes them from the schema diff (CatalogSchemaAdapter.ToEvolvableColumns), from the upsert column list, and from change detection.

keys.validation: Load time (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.MapTemporal / MapVersioning): rejected together with 'versioning.scd2.enabled: true' (two history mechanisms would record every change twice) and together with 'target.truncateBeforeLoad: true' (SQL Server does not allow TRUNCATE TABLE on a system-versioned table; legacy silently skipped the truncate, leaving the flow believing it had done a full reload when it had appended). Run time (IngestionFlowRunner.EnsureSupportedFeatures) repeats both for the control-DB and legacy load paths. Plan time (TemporalTablePlanner.Plan), before any DDL runs: the target must exist, must be a table not a view, and must have a PRIMARY KEY ("SQL Server requires a system-versioned table to have a PRIMARY KEY, and the target has none. Set 'target.identityColumn' ..."); a declared history table that differs from the live one is refused; a declared period column name that differs from an existing live period is refused (a period cannot be renamed in place); and a period column name that collides with a data column, on the live table or in the desired schema, is refused.

keys.description: Turn on system-versioned history for the target. Equivalent to the 'versioning.temporalHistory' shorthand, which is OR-ed with this value; a flow may set either.

keys.description: The schema holding the history table. It always resolves inside the TARGET's own database, because SQL Server accepts only a two-part history name. The default 'ver' is the schema legacy SQLFlow used via its flw.SysCFG 'Schema06Version' parameter, so a ported flow keeps its history where the old estate put it. The engine creates the schema when it is missing (an idempotent SCHEMA_ID-guarded CREATE SCHEMA, emitted as the first statement of the temporal batch).

SQL Server requires the history table to live in the same database as the target and accepts only a two-part name." A blank value falls back to the default.

keys.description: The history table's name. Null (the default) mirrors the target's own table name, which is what legacy did. Set it only when two targets in different schemas would otherwise collide on one history name inside the shared history schema. When the named table already exists (for example a history migrated from an older estate) SQL Server links it rather than creating one, validating column names and ordinals against the current table because the engine always enables with DATA_CONSISTENCY_CHECK = ON.

keys.description: The period's ROW START column, added as datetime2(periodPrecision) GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW START NOT NULL with a DEFAULT of DATEADD(SECOND, -1, SYSUTCDATETIME()). The one-second offset matters on a table that already holds rows: it puts every pre-existing row's period start strictly in the past, so the period is never empty and the row stays visible to FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF. This carries the legacy flw.GetVersioningScript semantic forward: history begins at the moment versioning was enabled.

keys.description: Declare the two period columns HIDDEN (the legacy behavior and the default), so SELECT *, result-set metadata, and every downstream consumer keep seeing the target's original column list. This is what makes enabling temporal history on a live table a NON-BREAKING change for its consumers. Set false to make the period columns part of the ordinary projection. Either way they remain GENERATED ALWAYS and unwritable, and either way sys.columns still reports them, which is why the engine filters on generated_always_type rather than on is_hidden.

keys.description: The datetime2 fractional-second scale (0-7) of the two period columns. The default is SQL Server's own datetime2 default of 7; legacy SQLFlow emitted 0, which cannot tell two updates to the same row inside one second apart. Set it to 0 when linking a history table migrated from a legacy estate, whose period columns must match the current table's types exactly. A flow sourced from the legacy control DB gets 0 automatically (IngestionFlowMapper.FromLegacy).

keys.description: HISTORY_RETENTION_PERIOD in days: history rows older than this are removed by the engine's background cleanup task. Null (the default) keeps history forever, which the engine renders explicitly as HISTORY_RETENTION_PERIOD = INFINITE, so clearing the setting on a later run returns the table to keeping history forever. Changing it is the ONE difference the temporal planner still acts on once a table is already versioned: re-issuing SET (SYSTEM_VERSIONING = ON ...) is the supported way to change the period, so that statement is emitted unguarded in this case. Requires an engine that supports retention: Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance, or SQL Server 2025 and later; elsewhere SQL Server rejects the option and the engine surfaces that rather than swallowing it.

Setting it currently has no observable effect on a run.

Computed projection-column declarations (a faithful port of legacy flw.IngestionVirtual rows), bound to List<IngestionVirtualColumnYaml> (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/IngestionYaml.cs:39) and mapped by YamlIngestionFlowLoader.MapVirtualColumns (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:460-483) into IngestionFlow.VirtualColumns (IReadOnlyList<VirtualColumn>, src/SqlFlow.Core/Ingestion/IngestionFlow.cs:70). Consumed entirely by IngestionSchemaBuilder.Build (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:40-76): it builds a name -> declaration lookup from every entry with a non-blank name (case-insensitive; when the list has duplicate names, only the FIRST declaration for that name is kept, IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:40-43), then walks the flow's INTROSPECTED SOURCE columns. A source column whose RAW (pre-schema.cleanColumnNames) name matches a declaration is re-marked Role=Virtual/Origin=Computed, its projection becomes that declaration's expression instead of the raw bulk-copied value, and it is excluded from the source-to-target bulk-copy name map, so it is neither read from the source nor treated as a data column for the upsert (though it still appears, computed, in the built target/staging schema). A declaration whose name matches no introspected source column, or that has no name at all, is never looked up and so silently contributes nothing to the built schema -- it is not an error. Because a virtualized column is excluded from the bulk-copy map, naming it (directly, or via matchKeys/versioning.scd2 resolving to it) as a key column fails schema-evolution's canonical-index planning with SqlFlowException "Key column '<name>' is not a bulk-copied target column (is it in IgnoreColumns or a virtual column?)." (IngestionFlowRunner.MapName, src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Ingestion/IngestionFlowRunner.cs:1157-1161) and fails upsert generation itself with "Key column '<name>' is not among the data columns." (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/UpsertGenerator.cs:143).

One computed-column declaration; binds IngestionVirtualColumnYaml {name, dataType, dataTypeExpression, expression} (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/IngestionYaml.cs:174-180) and maps to a VirtualColumn record (src/SqlFlow.Core/Ingestion/VirtualColumn.cs:7-21). Only expression is required; name, dataType, and dataTypeExpression are all optional and blank/whitespace values normalize to unset.
